product_contract.stable_matrix: docs/TEST_COVERAGE_MATRIX.md is the authoritative stable cross-layer scenario contract. Every active scenario records one stable ID, product name, independent Oracle, requiredness, coverage Owner, applicable layers, risk classification, and current representative source anchors.
product_contract.asset_inventory: docs/test-audit/TEST_ASSET_LEDGER.jsonl owns exhaustive per-method, target, runner, fixture, TestingSupport, dependency, consumer, and execution-entry mapping for the audited candidate.
product_contract.dynamic_evidence: Current execution observations and run history are published through the owning engineering handoff or active test-audit artifacts.
product_contract.update_rule: A scenario-contract change updates stable meaning and representative anchors; an executable-asset change refreshes the exhaustive ledger and source fingerprints.

publication_path: Product meaning is identified by one stable scenario ID and independent Oracle.
Risk classification determines required, conditional, and not-relevant responsibilities across six validation layers.
Representative current methods make each declared layer reviewable in the stable matrix.
The exhaustive ledger resolves every current test method, target, runner, fixture, TestingSupport dependency, consumer, and execution entry point.
Current execution results remain in candidate-specific handoffs or audit evidence so they can change without redefining the stable contract.

test_meaning_conclusion.classification: retain all 22 stable product scenarios and all 846 current executable test methods; publish their distinct stable-contract and exhaustive-inventory roles
test_meaning_conclusion.protected_meaning: Layer selection is reconstructible from product Oracle, requiredness, Owner, and risk before current pass/fail evidence is read.
test_meaning_conclusion.neighboring_meaning: Test assertions, fixture topology, runner transport, and product behavior remain owned by their executable slices.
independent_oracle: Each stable scenario preserves the product Oracle reconstructed at C0.
Every representative method resolves to one active source declaration, matches its ledger layer, and maps back to the scenario.
Every one of the 846 source test methods resolves to one ledger row with matching target, path, line, and method-body fingerprint.
Every active stable scenario retains at least one executable consumer.

test_quality_conclusion.fail_sensitivity: The validator rejects duplicate assets or symbols, missing source declarations, body-fingerprint drift, target or source-line drift, unknown dependencies, incomplete six-layer classification, missing consumers, stale anchors, dynamic matrix status markers, and broken links.
test_quality_conclusion.fixture_fidelity: Fixture and runner assets remain executable-ledger dependencies; the stable matrix names their required responsibility without converting candidate-specific outcomes into stable meaning.
test_quality_conclusion.isolation: The candidate changes tracked documentation and audit data only. Private generation and validation tools remain under the ignored audit evidence root.
test_quality_conclusion.flake_assessment: Closure is deterministic source and contract reconciliation with no timing, process, permission, or UI dependency.
test_quality_conclusion.target_reachability: Source discovery found 42 FlowTabCoreTests, 696 FlowTabTests, and 108 FlowTabUITests methods, each matched by one ledger row.
